dataforseo.title: Best DataForSEO Alternatives and Competitors in 2026
dataforseo.lead: The best DataForSEO alternatives for scraping AI search engines and SERPs are Cloro, BrightData, SearchApi, Oxylabs, and Olostep. In continuous production testing across consumer AI surfaces, Cloro is the most reliable overall (100% success rate across all six surfaces), while BrightData ($10 minimum) and Oxylabs (~$0.15 per prompt/month at scale) beat DataForSEO on price. If you want a full open-source AI visibility platform instead of raw API endpoints, you can self-host Elmo for free and plug in keys from DataForSEO or any of its competitors.
dataforseo.elmoPitch: DataForSEO gives you raw JSON endpoints, which means you still have to build scheduling, mention detection, citation parsing, sentiment scoring, and historical dashboards yourself. Elmo is an open-source (MIT) AI visibility platform you can self-host for free—or run on Elmo Cloud from $29/mo—that already integrates DataForSEO, Cloro, BrightData, Oxylabs, SearchApi, and Olostep out of the box. Bring your own API keys, avoid per-seat pricing, and inspect every line of the scoring logic.

sections.heading: Why Teams Look for a DataForSEO Alternative
paragraphs: [DataForSEO](https://try.dataforseo.com/elmo) is a strong pay-as-you-go API and one of the providers we support in Elmo. In our production monitoring across 4,213 runs, it tied for second in overall reliability at 95% and recorded the fastest median latency (11 seconds). It is also the only provider in our stack that fronts both live UI scrapers (ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Mode, Google AI Overviews) and direct model APIs behind a single account.

Teams still look for DataForSEO competitors for four concrete reasons. First, surface coverage: DataForSEO does not scrape Microsoft Copilot and has no live UI scraper for Perplexity, serving Perplexity through its LLM Responses model API instead. Second, unit cost: at roughly $1.20 per tracked prompt per month (assuming five runs a day across ChatGPT and Google AI Mode), it costs nearly twice as much as [Cloro](https://cloro.dev?fpr=elmo&fp_sid=dataforseo-alternatives) (~$0.65) and nearly three times as much as [BrightData](https://get.brightdata.com/elmo?sid=dataforseo-alternatives) (~$0.45). Third, prompt length and localization constraints: DataForSEO limits prompt text to 500 characters, and country localization support differs by surface. Fourth, some marketing teams realize they do not want to build a custom tracker on top of a raw API at all, and would rather use a turnkey [AI visibility tool](/blog/best-ai-visibility-tools).
Note: Provider links on this page are Elmo affiliate links. Rankings and reliability numbers come from repeated automated testing published live on our [status page](/status).

sections.heading: DataForSEO vs. Top API Competitors: Measured Comparison
paragraphs: Most AI referral traffic comes from ChatGPT and Google AI Mode, and neither exposes a public API for the consumer UI. Calling a model API with web search enabled does not reproduce what customers actually see, because the consumer product adds its own retrieval, ranking, and formatting layers. To measure [real UI answers](/ai-visibility-tools/features/real-ui-answers) and [query fan-out](/features/query-fan-out), you need a scraping API.

Elmo runs all six providers continuously in production. Cost estimates below normalize each vendor's pricing to a standard workload: tracking one prompt five times a day across ChatGPT and Google AI Mode (about 300 evaluations per month). For a deeper breakdown of per-surface pass rates, read our benchmark of the [best LLM scraping APIs](/blog/best-llm-scraping-apis).

sections.heading: Closer Look at the 5 Best DataForSEO API Alternatives
paragraphs: Each scraping API makes different trade-offs between billing model, surface coverage, and connection handling. All five below are supported in Elmo's [provider configuration](/docs/user-guide/providers).

items.title: 1. Cloro — Best Overall Reliability and Coverage
items.body: [Cloro](https://cloro.dev?fpr=elmo&fp_sid=dataforseo-alternatives) is the most reliable provider we have measured, hitting 100% across ChatGPT, Google AI Mode, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, Perplexity, and Copilot. It uses an asynchronous task API that meters concurrency cleanly and does not charge for failed requests. It is the primary provider powering Elmo Cloud, and is also used by Ahrefs, Scrunch, and Evertune. Plans start at $30/mo using credit-based billing (Perplexity costs 3 credits, Gemini and AI Mode 4, Copilot and AI Overview 5, ChatGPT 7).

items.title: 2. BrightData — Best Low-Cost Pay-As-You-Go Alternative
items.body: If you like DataForSEO's pay-as-you-go model but want lower unit costs and full six-surface coverage, [BrightData](https://get.brightdata.com/elmo?sid=dataforseo-alternatives) starts with a $10 minimum and costs roughly $0.45 per prompt per month. It reaches all six surfaces via dataset collectors and its SERP API, clearing 96–98% reliability everywhere except Google AI Overviews, where it drops to 71%.

items.title: 3. SearchApi — Best for Synchronous Requests and Flat Pricing
items.body: Unlike asynchronous queue APIs that require polling, [SearchApi](https://www.searchapi.io/?via=elmo) serves all six AI surfaces from a single synchronous GET endpoint, with flat pricing per successful search ($4 per 1,000 on the $40/mo plan, dropping to $1 per 1,000 at high volume) and 100 free searches on sign-up. Keep in mind that when Google loads an AI Overview asynchronously via a page token, redeeming that token requires a second search call.

items.title: 4. Oxylabs — Cheapest Per-Run Scraping at High Volume
items.body: At roughly $0.15 per prompt per month ($0.50 per 1,000 results on the $49/mo Micro plan), [Oxylabs](https://oxylabs.go2cloud.org/aff_c?offer_id=7&aff_id=2263&url_id=32) is about eight times cheaper per run than DataForSEO. The trade-offs are strict: there is no pay-as-you-go tier, it cannot scrape Gemini or Copilot, and its 83% overall reliability leaves unrecoverable gaps in historical time-series data.

items.title: 5. Olostep — Built for High-Volume Batch Workloads
items.body: [Olostep](https://olostep.com/?ref=elmo) is a pay-as-you-go scraper covering all six surfaces and used by enterprise AEO platforms like Profound, AthenaHQ, and AirOps. While its API is ergonomic for high-throughput batch jobs, it is the most expensive option (~$2.25 per prompt/month), the slowest (58s median latency, with tail runs near 19 minutes), and scored 82% overall reliability in our monitoring.

sections.heading: Direct Model APIs vs. Consumer UI Scrapers
paragraphs: One reason developers choose DataForSEO is that a single account lets you switch between live UI scraping and its LLM Responses API by pinning a model version (for example, gpt-5.5 or gemini-2.5-flash). If you only use DataForSEO for model-level responses rather than live UI scraping, you do not need another scraper—you can call the upstream model APIs directly.

Calling the OpenAI API, Anthropic API, Mistral API, or OpenRouter with web search enabled is faster and avoids scraper maintenance. On OpenRouter, perplexity/sonar costs $1 per million tokens plus $0.005 per request, making it the cheapest programmatic way to approximate Perplexity. Similarly, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Mistral APIs all return [query fan-out](/ai-visibility-tools/features/query-fan-out) searches.

However, model APIs are not substitutes for consumer UI scraping when accuracy matters. As we found when analyzing [ChatGPT UI vs. OpenAI API citations](/blog/chatgpt-ui-reddit-citations-api), the consumer apps apply distinct retrieval layers, product cards, and domain weights. In Elmo, most teams use a scraper like Cloro or DataForSEO for ChatGPT and Google AI Mode, and add an OpenRouter or Anthropic key to cover Claude and Grok.

sections.heading: How to Choose Between DataForSEO and Its Competitors
paragraphs: If you are tracking 25 or more prompts and want a single integration that covers all six AI surfaces without dropped runs, choose [Cloro](https://cloro.dev?fpr=elmo&fp_sid=dataforseo-alternatives). Its $30/mo floor is quickly offset by its 100% pass rate across Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, and Perplexity, and you never pay for failed requests.

If you are tracking fewer than 20 prompts or running occasional audits and refuse to pay a monthly subscription, stick with [DataForSEO](https://try.dataforseo.com/elmo) ($50 minimum top-up) or switch to [BrightData](https://get.brightdata.com/elmo?sid=dataforseo-alternatives) ($10 minimum). Choose BrightData if you need real Perplexity and Copilot UI scraping; keep DataForSEO if you care about fast 11-second median turnaround times or Google AI Overview reliability (where DataForSEO scores 89% vs. BrightData's 71%).

If you want to stop maintaining scraper parsers altogether, deploy Elmo. Because Elmo supports [bring your own keys](/ai-visibility-tools/features/bring-your-own-keys) for all six scraping providers plus direct model APIs, you can switch from DataForSEO to Cloro or BrightData by changing a single environment variable (SCRAPE_TARGETS), while getting full [citation analytics](/features/citation-tracking), competitor share of voice, and an [API and MCP server](/features/api-and-mcp) out of the box.

faqs.question: What is the best DataForSEO alternative for AI search tracking?
faqs.answer: Cloro is the best overall alternative to DataForSEO for scraping AI search engines. In continuous testing across ChatGPT, Google AI Mode, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, Perplexity, and Microsoft Copilot, Cloro achieved a 100% success rate at roughly half the per-prompt cost of DataForSEO (~$0.65 vs. ~$1.20 per prompt per month). For teams that prefer pay-as-you-go billing without a monthly subscription, BrightData is the closest alternative with a $10 minimum.

faqs.question: Is there a free or open-source alternative to DataForSEO?
faqs.answer: Every SERP and LLM scraping API charges for proxy and browser infrastructure, though SearchApi includes 100 free searches on sign-up and BrightData starts at a $10 pay-as-you-go minimum. However, if you are paying for DataForSEO to power an internal AI visibility tracker, the software layer has a free, open-source alternative: Elmo. You can self-host Elmo under the MIT license for $0 and plug in your own scraping or model API keys at cost.

faqs.question: Which DataForSEO competitor is best for monitoring Google AI Overviews?
faqs.answer: Google AI Overviews is the hardest surface for scrapers to capture reliably. In our production benchmarks, Cloro led with a 100% success rate on Google AI Overviews, followed by DataForSEO at 89% and Olostep at 84%. BrightData and Oxylabs both dropped to 71% on Google AI Overviews despite performing well on other surfaces.

faqs.question: How does DataForSEO pricing compare to Oxylabs, BrightData, and Cloro?
faqs.answer: Tracking a single prompt five times a day across ChatGPT and Google AI Mode (300 runs a month) costs roughly $1.20 on DataForSEO and SearchApi, $0.65 on Cloro, $0.45 on BrightData, $0.15 on Oxylabs, and $2.25 on Olostep. However, plan minimums change the math at small scale: Oxylabs requires a $49/mo plan and Cloro starts at $30/mo, whereas DataForSEO ($50 top-up) and BrightData ($10 top-up) bill strictly pay-as-you-go.

faqs.question: Why does DataForSEO miss Perplexity and Microsoft Copilot UI answers?
faqs.answer: DataForSEO does not offer a live UI scraper for Microsoft Copilot or Perplexity. While it scrapes the real consumer interfaces for ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Mode, and Google AI Overviews, it routes Perplexity requests through its LLM Responses API, which queries the underlying model API rather than the consumer web app. If you need live UI scraping for Perplexity and Copilot, use Cloro, BrightData, SearchApi, or Olostep.
